I'm 37, been farming since I was a little girl. No schooling, but I know my land. My husband works construction in the county town, sends money when he can but it's not steady. We have six people in the house — my mother-in-law, husband, me, and two children in school. School costs money, so I have to be careful with every yuan.

I farm 10 mu, all wheat-maize double crop. This year I'll do about the same as last year. Last year was okay, not great but we got by. Change is risky when you don't have savings.

For wheat, I saved my own seed from last year. No need to buy. I'll plant after National Day, around October 8th, same as my neighbors. First I plow the field after the maize comes off, then sow the wheat. For fertilizer, I put one bag of compound for every two and a half mu — that's about 40 jin per mu — and spread it by hand before planting. The fertilizer dealer always says use more, but I don't have that money. My neighbor Aunt Li uses about the same and her wheat is fine. In March when the wheat turns green, I'll topdress with urea, about 30 jin per mu. If the wheat looks yellow I'll add a bit more, if it looks green maybe a bit less. I don't calculate — I look and decide.

Water is expensive, 20 yuan each time to pump. I'll water before winter if it's dry, and once more in spring when it turns green. If it's very dry at heading maybe one more, but that costs too much. I use herbicide after planting, but I don't spray insecticide unless I see bugs — that saves money.

For maize, the wheat comes off in early June and I have to plant right away, sometimes within two or three days. I hire a tractor with a planter — costs money but it's fast. I buy hybrid seed, 55 yuan per mu, can't avoid that. Saved maize seed doesn't work. I put compound fertilizer in the planting row, about 40 jin per mu. Then if July is dry I'll side-dress some urea, maybe 20 jin per mu. If it rains well I might skip it to save cash. Maize needs less water than wheat, maybe one irrigation, two only if it's very dry.

My mother-in-law can help cook but can't do heavy work. My children are in school. So most of the work is on me. I hire a few people for wheat harvest and maize planting when it's busy — those are the times you can't be late.

I hope for 400 kg per mu of wheat and 450 kg of maize, but you never know. Weather decides. I'll do what I can with what I have.
